facts.text: The Lodge at Primland sits on 12,000 private acres above the Dan River Gorge in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia.
facts.excerpt: luxury Blue Ridge Mountains resort on 12,000 private acres above the Dan River Gorge in Virginia.

facts.text: The Tree Houses were designed in France by the treehouse architectural firm La Cabane Perchee and built of aromatic red cedar.
facts.excerpt: Designed in France by renowned treehouse architectural firm La Cabane Perchee – and built of aromatic red cedar

facts.text: Tree House guests receive a complimentary daily continental breakfast delivered to their door.
facts.excerpt: Tree Houses suit up to two adults, who also receive a complimentary daily continental breakfast delivered to their door

facts.text: Accessing the Tree Houses requires a four-wheel drive vehicle, and complimentary shuttle services are available for guests without one.
facts.excerpt: Accessing the Tree Houses requires a four-wheel drive vehicle. For guests who do not have four-wheel drive, complimentary shuttle services are available.

facts.text: The Lodge rooms and suites have deep soaking tubs, private balconies, sliding floor-to-ceiling windows and Frette sheets.
facts.excerpt: deep soaking tubs, impeccable views, private balconies, sliding floor-to-ceiling windows and Frette sheets

facts.text: Fairway Cottages sit along the golf course and have cathedral ceilings and living areas with Tennessee fieldstone fireplaces.
facts.excerpt: Located along the golf course with stunning jade and sapphire-hued mountain views, fairway accommodations offer hardwood floors, cathedral ceilings and cozy living areas with Tennessee fieldstone fireplaces.

facts.text: Eleven Rustic Mountain Homes at the Sporting Club have wraparound decks, outdoor hot tubs and stone fireplaces.
facts.excerpt: 11 Rustic Mountain Homes offer blissful solitude and the rugged back-to-nature romance of the Blue Ridge Plateau in comfort.

facts.text: The Highland Course is an 18-hole championship golf course set across the ridges and valleys of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
facts.excerpt: The Highland Course is Primland

facts.text: The Primland Sporting Club offers sporting clays, archery and air rifle, with guides and instruction.
facts.excerpt: Guests can experience activities including sporting clays, archery and air rifle, with expert guides and instruction available for beginners and experienced participants alike.

facts.text: The resort has an on-property observatory, and Condé Nast Traveler describes nightly guided stargazing sessions there.
facts.excerpt: nightly guided stargazing in the observatory

facts.text: Stables Saloon is on the second floor of Primland's former horse stables, regularly hosts live bluegrass concerts and is part of the Crooked Road: Virginia's Heritage Music Trail.
facts.excerpt: Climb the stairs to the secluded second floor of Primland’s former horse stables

facts.text: Stables Saloon serves a Southern supper family-style.
facts.excerpt: Served family-style

facts.text: The Schlumberger Wine Cellar in The Lodge is named for the sister property Domaines Schlumberger in Alsace, France.
facts.excerpt: Named for sister property – Domaines Schlumberger – in Alsace, France

facts.text: Leatherflower is the main restaurant and offers a culinary journey through the tastes of Appalachia.
facts.excerpt: provide an idyllic setting for a culinary journey through the tastes of Appalachia

facts.text: The indoor heated swimming pool is chlorine-free.
facts.excerpt: The indoor heated swimming pool is chlorine-free

facts.text: Sage, Wellbeing by Auberge, is the resort's spa and wellbeing destination, inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains.
facts.excerpt: Sage, Wellbeing by Auberge, is both a physical space and holistic experience drawing inspiration from the quiet power of the land.

facts.text: Complimentary wellness classes are offered, including yoga, mat Pilates, meditation and Chi-Gong.
facts.excerpt: Indoor Yoga

facts.text: The Junior Mountaineers Kids Club is for children ages 6-12 and includes pond-fishing, foraging, archery and horseback riding.
facts.excerpt: Kids ages 6-12 embark on a journey through nature-based experiences ranging from pond-fishing to foraging and archery to horseback riding.

facts.text: The resort is about a two-hour drive north of Charlotte.
facts.excerpt: about two hours north of Charlotte

facts.text: Private airport transportation is available for a fee upon request.
facts.excerpt: private airport transportation is available for a fee upon request.

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler says guests who want to go off property would need a car of their own.
facts.excerpt: If you are interested in going off property, you'd definitely need a car of your own.

facts.text: The 12,000 acres were originally purchased in 1977 by the French oil magnate Didier Primat.
facts.excerpt: originally purchased in 1977 by the French oil magnate, Didier Primat

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler lists the resort among its Readers' Choice Awards winners from 2016 through 2026.
